name: Tiotropium
summary: Once-daily long-acting antimuscarinic that sustains bronchodilation for over 24 h and reduces COPD exacerbations.
mechanism: Long-acting competitive antagonist at muscarinic receptors with kinetic selectivity for M3 — slow dissociation underlies the >24 h bronchodilator effect.

dosing.adult: HandiHaler 18 mcg once daily, or Respimat 5 mcg (2 puffs) once daily
dosing.renalAdjustment: No adjustment for mild-moderate renal impairment; monitor if severe

safety.pregnancy: Limited human data; inhaled use generally considered acceptable if clearly indicated
safety.lactation: No human data; inhaled doses give minimal systemic exposure — weigh benefit
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to tiotropium, ipratropium, or atropine derivatives
Severe milk protein allergy (HandiHaler capsules contain lactose)
warnings: Urinary retention, especially with prostatic hyperplasia
monitoring: Anticholinergic side effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary symptoms)

indications: Add-on therapy for moderate-to-severe asthma (6 years and older)
clinicalPearls: Once-daily dosing improves adherence and reduces COPD exacerbations
Full bronchodilator effect may take several days to a week
good: 24-hour bronchodilation from a single daily dose, with exacerbation reduction in COPD
bad: Acute bronchospasm relief (slow onset); narrow-angle glaucoma or urinary retention
